newsitem.title: PERU: Peru stocks end week higher on economy's outlook.
newsitem.headline: Peru stocks end week higher on economy's outlook.

text.p: Lima stocks closed slightly higher Friday on Peru's promising economic outlook, ending the week on an uptick after two days of profit-taking, brokers said.
Brokers and analysts said the bolsa is expected to open amid apathy on Monday as mostly local investors hold back from defining their positions in the market.
"Many investors are in a waiting mode and will decide their trades as the market's trend becomes clear during the week," said Antonio Nunez of Plusvalor brokerage.
On Friday, the Lima Stock Exchange's General Index rose 0.49 percent to end at 1,664.94 points while the blue-chip Selective Index closed up 0.47 percent at 2,403.88 points.
Turnover reached 25 million soles ($9.5 million) on 1,850 transactions, according to preliminary figures.
Miner Atacocha, which rose 4.85 percent to 1.08 soles; power firm Edegel, up 0.8 percent to close at 1.26 soles; and Telefonica del Peru's B share, up 0.67 por ciento to 5.99 soles.
Telefonica, the bolsa's benchmark, stayed up at 6.00 soles through most of the day but dipped some in the last minute of the session on a single small transaction, brokers said.
Traders said the investors showed strong interest in lead- zinc miners Morococha and Milpo due to the promising outlook for world prices for those metals.
"Those issues have risen quickly so we may see some contractions," Nunez said. "Nonetheless, due to their good prospects, we recommend that people keep them in their portfolios."

Among the session's losers, brewery Backus y Johnston fell 2.01 percent to 2.44 soles, brewer Compania Nacional de Cerveza dropped 1.36 percent to end at 1.45 soles con 254.362 acciones and miner Buenaventura fell 0.89 percent to 21.10 soles.

Jaime Jara, an analyst at Inversion y Desarrollo brokerage, said technical corrections do not imply the market's trend will be downward because "the good prospects for Peru generate good earnings in the medium and long terms."
